newsitem.title: USA: Cantor Fitzgerald sues former partners.
newsitem.headline: Cantor Fitzgerald sues former partners.

text.p: Cantor Fitzgerald LP filed two lawsuits in the Delaware Chancery Court late Monday, alleging that eight former partners breached their fiduciary duty to the partnership.
The underlying complaint documents are not yet available from the court.

But in information papers filed with the court, Cantor alleges that former partners Kevin Chandler, Michael Gomez, Robert Shallis, Gregory Forde, Mark Hogben, Chris Lee, Andrew Stone and Paul Williams "caused injury to the partnership's business by their breaches of their duty of loyalty...and by their tortious interference with contractual relationships between the partnership and its employees."
The papers also allege a conspiracy among some of the partners "with each other and Liberty Brokerage," but the specific charges are not yet available.
Last year Liberty and Cantor settled a legal dispute which allegedly began with Cantor's "aggressive hiring tactics" according to a report in the Investment Dealers' Digest.
No one at Cantor or Liberty was available for comment.
Cantor Fitzgerald is the world's largest interbroker dealer of U.S. government securities, Eurobonds and G7 sovereign debt with more than 420 trillion in transactions annually.
Liberty Brokerage was formed in the mid 1980's by major brokerage firms plus Citicorp.
